content:
AIYANA BROOKS-TAN
[EMAIL] | [PHONE] | [PORTFOLIO / GITHUB]

PROFESSIONAL SUMMARY
Computing student with practical experience building accessible web applications using React and TypeScript. Developed a full-stack final-year project with a Node.js/Express API and PostgreSQL, and contributed accessibility fixes and React components during a software development internship. Experience includes screen-reader testing, automated testing, and frontend work on collaborative projects.

TECHNICAL SKILLS
Frontend: React, TypeScript, JavaScript, Next.js, Tailwind CSS, responsive web development, web accessibility
Backend and data: Node.js, Express, PostgreSQL, Firebase Authentication
Testing and documentation: Jest, React Testing Library, Storybook, screen-reader testing (NVDA, VoiceOver)
Other: Chart.js, Vercel, Markdown

EXPERIENCE
Software Development Intern | Harbourline Media | May 2024 – Aug 2024
- Worked on accessibility fixes and React components for a news website.
- Built a keyboard- and screen-reader-friendly image gallery for article pages and documented it in Storybook.
- Used React, Storybook, Jest, and React Testing Library.

Teaching Assistant, First-Year Web Development Lab | Spring 2025
- Supported approximately 30 students during one semester of web development lab sessions.

PROJECTS
Tidewatch — Final-Year Project | 2024–2025
- Built an accessible web app for sea swimmers showing tides, water temperature, and weather around the Irish coast.
- Developed the frontend with React and TypeScript, a Node.js/Express API that caches data from public weather and tide APIs, and PostgreSQL storage for user favourites.
- Tested the app with NVDA and VoiceOver; achieved a Lighthouse accessibility score of 100.
- Received a grade of 82% (First Class) and demonstrated the project at the college project showcase.
- Technologies: React, TypeScript, Node.js, Express, PostgreSQL, Chart.js, Jest.

Yoga Studio Booking Site — Freelance | 2025
- Built marketing pages and a class timetable with booking requests sent by email.
- Used static generation with Next.js; deployed the site on Vercel and enabled content editing through Markdown files.
- Technologies: Next.js, React, Tailwind CSS, Vercel.

Accessible Gallery Component — Harbourline Media Internship | 2024
- Created a keyboard- and screen-reader-friendly image gallery component for article pages and documented it in Storybook.
- Technologies: React, Storybook, Jest, React Testing Library.

Study Buddy — Group Project | 2023
- Built the React frontend and login screens for a student team project matching classmates for study sessions.
- Worked in a four-student team; other team members developed the API and database.
- Technologies: React, JavaScript, Firebase Authentication.

ADDITIONAL EXPERIENCE
Social Media Volunteer | Sea Swimming Club
- Run social media for a sea swimming club.

Barista | Part-time during college

EDUCATION
Liffey Institute of Technology
Computing — Third-year student

critique.content_quality_feedback: The CV is well structured, readable, and professionally targeted toward junior frontend/full-stack work. The strongest evidence is concrete: React and TypeScript projects, Node.js/Express and PostgreSQL work, accessibility testing with NVDA and VoiceOver, a Lighthouse accessibility score of 100, and Storybook/Jest experience. The main content weaknesses are that the contact details and portfolio link are still placeholders, the internship and project sections partially duplicate the same gallery work, and some bullets could distinguish professional experience from student or freelance projects more clearly. The CV is credible for a junior candidate, but it should not imply the level of professional experience requested by this role.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The headings, reverse-chronological experience format, standard section names, and plain-text technology lists are ATS-friendly. Relevant terms such as React, TypeScript, Node.js, Express, PostgreSQL, Jest, React Testing Library, Next.js, accessibility, Storybook, and Firebase Authentication are present. However, the placeholders '[EMAIL]', '[PHONE]' and '[PORTFOLIO / GITHUB]' would prevent effective recruiter contact and limit screening value. The CV does not show Git, end-to-end testing, semantic HTML, OWASP Top 10, or privacy terminology; these are genuine candidate-evidence gaps rather than terms that should be added without support. The phrase 'automated testing' should be qualified because the document only demonstrates Jest and React Testing Library, not end-to-end testing.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The document aligns well with the role's React/TypeScript focus, accessibility emphasis, Node.js/Express and PostgreSQL project work, Next.js, Storybook, and wellness-related experience through the yoga studio site. The Tidewatch project is particularly relevant because it demonstrates an end-to-end web application, API integration, SQL storage, accessibility testing, and performance/accessibility measurement. The candidate's material does not demonstrate 2+ years of professional React/TypeScript experience; the available professional internship lasted approximately four months. It also does not demonstrate end-to-end testing, Git-based workflows, OWASP Top 10 awareness, health-data privacy experience, AWS/Docker, German/Croatian, or analytics/A/B testing. Fluent English is evidenced by the original English application letter but is not stated in the CV. The CV's accessibility focus aligns strongly with Verdane Care's patient-first and accessibility priorities, but the overall profile is more consistent with a junior candidate than with the advertised must-have experience level.
critique.improvement_instructions:
CRITICAL ISSUES
1. In the contact header, replace '[EMAIL]', '[PHONE]' and '[PORTFOLIO / GITHUB]' with the candidate's actual professional email address, phone number, and portfolio/GitHub URL. Ensure the URL is written in full plain text so ATS and recruiters can parse it.
2. In the Technical Skills section under 'Other' or 'Frontend', remove 'responsive web development' unless the candidate can substantiate that experience from the original material. The supplied candidate information does not explicitly support this claim. Do not replace it with another unsupported skill.
3. In the Professional Summary, change 'Experience includes screen-reader testing, automated testing, and frontend work on collaborative projects' to 'Experience includes screen-reader testing, unit/component testing with Jest and React Testing Library, and frontend work on collaborative projects.' This accurately reflects the evidence provided and avoids implying end-to-end testing.

MINOR, HIGH-VALUE IMPROVEMENTS
4. In the Professional Summary, change 'Developed a full-stack final-year project' to 'Built a full-stack final-year project' or 'Built a full-stack student project' so the document clearly distinguishes project experience from professional full-stack employment.
5. In the Projects section, avoid repeating the Accessible Gallery Component as a separate project immediately after describing the same work under Harbourline Media. Either remove the duplicate project entry or retain it but label the internship bullet as the primary experience and use the project entry only if it adds distinct implementation or testing detail.
6. In the Education section, change 'Computing — Third-year student' to 'Computing, Third Year | Expected graduation: [month/year]' only if the expected graduation date is known. Do not invent a date. This would make the candidate's current academic status easier for recruiters and ATS systems to interpret.
7. Add a short 'Languages' section after Technical Skills stating 'English — Fluent' if this accurately reflects the candidate's proficiency, which is supported by the original English application letter.
8. In the Teaching Assistant entry, replace 'Supported approximately 30 students during one semester of web development lab sessions' with 'Supported approximately 30 first-year students across one semester of web development lab sessions.' This uses the fuller evidence already provided and gives the mentoring experience more relevance to the role.
critique.critical_issues:
1. Potential unsupported claim: 'responsive web development' appears in Technical Skills, but the Original Candidate Information does not explicitly establish this skill. Remove it unless substantiated.
2. Potentially misleading testing wording: 'automated testing' in the Professional Summary may imply end-to-end testing, while the Original Candidate Information supports Jest and React Testing Library but not end-to-end testing. Qualify the wording as unit/component testing.
3. Unusable contact information: the header contains placeholders rather than actual contact details and a working portfolio/GitHub link. Replace them before submitting.
Claims the sources (the candidate's own material; for the employer, the job ad and company research) do not support:
- "responsive web development"

critique.content_quality_feedback: The CV is clearly structured, concise, and professionally targeted toward frontend/full-stack web development. The Professional Summary gives a useful overview of React, TypeScript, Node.js, Express, PostgreSQL, accessibility, and testing experience. Project descriptions are particularly strong because they explain the candidate's contribution, technologies, and outcomes, including a Lighthouse accessibility score of 100 and an 82% First Class result. The document also presents the candidate honestly as a student with project-based backend experience rather than overstating professional seniority. Main content weaknesses are the lack of measurable detail in some experience bullets, the very brief Additional Experience section, and contact fields that remain placeholders. There is also one potentially unsupported claim: "English — Fluent" is not explicitly stated in the Original Candidate Information.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The CV uses standard, ATS-friendly headings, plain text, conventional chronology, and searchable technology keywords. The skills are grouped logically and include many relevant terms from the advert: React, TypeScript, Node.js, Express, PostgreSQL, accessibility, Jest, Storybook, Next.js, Firebase Authentication, and Vercel. ATS alignment would be stronger if the CV explicitly used supported terms such as automated unit testing, screen-reader testing, authentication, static generation, and accessibility testing in context rather than relying mainly on the skills list. The document does not show Git-based workflows, end-to-end testing, semantic HTML, responsive layouts, OWASP Top 10, Docker, AWS, or healthcare privacy; these are candidate-profile gaps or unsupported areas rather than wording defects. The placeholder contact details and portfolio/GitHub field are a practical ATS and recruiter-usability problem because the application cannot be readily contacted or verified.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The CV is a credible and relevant early-career match for the role's React/TypeScript, Node.js/Express, PostgreSQL, accessibility, Next.js, Storybook, testing, and English-language requirements. Tidewatch is especially relevant: it demonstrates an end-to-end application with a React/TypeScript frontend, a Node.js/Express API, PostgreSQL storage, third-party API integration, screen-reader testing, and strong accessibility results. The Yoga Studio project gives the CV a wellness-related connection, although it is not healthcare or regulated-environment experience. The candidate does not meet or does not demonstrate the advertised 2+ years of professional React/TypeScript experience; their professional internship lasted approximately four months, while other experience is academic, freelance, or project-based. The document also does not demonstrate end-to-end testing, Git workflows, semantic HTML, responsive layouts, OWASP Top 10 awareness, health-data privacy knowledge, German/Croatian, AWS/Docker, or analytics/A-B testing. These are profile gaps, not defects that can be solved by rewriting. The strongest positioning is as a promising junior full-stack/frontend candidate with unusually strong accessibility and relevant project-based backend experience.
critique.improvement_instructions:
CRITICAL:
1. In the contact header, replace `[EMAIL]`, `[PHONE]`, and `[PORTFOLIO / GITHUB]` with the candidate's actual professional contact details and a working portfolio, GitHub, or project URL. Do not leave placeholders in the submitted CV.
2. In the Languages section, remove `English — Fluent` unless the candidate can substantiate that exact proficiency statement. The Original Candidate Information does not explicitly state English fluency. If accurate and supportable, retain it; otherwise use only a truthful language description supported by the candidate's information.

MINOR, HIGH-VALUE ENHANCEMENTS:

For example, change `Used React, Storybook, Jest, and React Testing Library.` to `Implemented React components and accessibility fixes; documented components in Storybook and used Jest and React Testing Library for automated unit/component testing.`
4. In the Tidewatch project entry, make the end-to-end nature and third-party integration more explicit. Change the second bullet to: `Built the application end to end: developed the React/TypeScript frontend, a Node.js/Express backend service that caches data from third-party weather and tide APIs, and PostgreSQL storage for user favourites.`
5. In the Study Buddy project entry, make the supported authentication experience more searchable. Change `Built the React frontend and login screens for a student team project matching classmates for study sessions.` to `Built the React frontend and authentication/login screens for a student team project matching classmates for study sessions, using Firebase Authentication.`
6. In the Professional Summary, avoid implying that all backend experience is professional. Replace `Built a full-stack final-year project with a Node.js/Express API and PostgreSQL` with `Built a full-stack final-year project using a Node.js/Express API and PostgreSQL` so the CV remains precise about the source of the experience.

critique.content_quality_feedback: This is a clear, well-structured early-career CV with strong project detail, relevant technologies, and credible evidence of accessibility work. The Tidewatch project is particularly effective because it demonstrates React/TypeScript, Node.js/Express, PostgreSQL, API integration, testing, and a measurable accessibility result. The main content weakness is that the CV presents a strong junior/student profile but does not clearly distinguish professional experience from academic and freelance projects. It also omits contact details, portfolio/GitHub links, project URLs, and dates for some education and additional experience, reducing completeness and recruiter usability. The Teaching Assistant entry is too brief to show the transferable mentoring and communication value.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The document uses ATS-friendly headings, plain text formatting, standard date conventions, and searchable technology names. Keyword coverage is strong for React, TypeScript, Node.js, Express, PostgreSQL, Jest, React Testing Library, Next.js, Storybook, accessibility, and Firebase Authentication. However, it does not show Git-based workflows, end-to-end testing, semantic HTML, responsive layouts, OWASP Top 10, privacy/GDPR, or English fluency explicitly. These should not be added unless supported by the candidate's experience. The absence of contact information and portfolio/GitHub URLs is a significant practical weakness. Estimated AI/ATS screening probability: moderate, approximately 65–75%, because the CV matches the technical stack but does not satisfy or evidence several must-have requirements, especially the 2+ years of professional experience and security/testing requirements.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The CV aligns well with the product's accessibility focus and core frontend/full-stack technologies. It demonstrates React and TypeScript, a Node.js/Express backend, PostgreSQL, third-party API integration, automated unit/component testing, screen-reader testing, Storybook, Next.js, and wellness-related work through the yoga studio site. It also shows mentoring potential through the Teaching Assistant role. The candidate's material does not demonstrate 2+ years of professional React/TypeScript experience; the internship lasted approximately four months and the remaining experience is academic, freelance, or personal. It also does not demonstrate end-to-end testing, Git workflows, semantic HTML, responsive layouts, OWASP Top 10 awareness, health-data privacy, AWS, Docker, analytics/A-B testing, German, or Croatian. These are candidate-experience gaps rather than defects that rewriting can solve. The CV should therefore position the candidate accurately as an early-career/junior full-stack or frontend developer rather than implying they already meet the seniority threshold.
critique.improvement_instructions:
CRITICAL / HIGH PRIORITY
1. In the Professional Summary, make the experience level explicit so the document does not imply 2+ years of professional engineering experience. For example, change the opening to: "Third-year Computing student and junior web developer with professional internship experience and hands-on project experience building accessible applications with React and TypeScript." Retain the Node.js/Express and PostgreSQL evidence, but describe Tidewatch as a final-year project rather than presenting it as equivalent to professional experience.
2. At the top of the CV, add the candidate's actual email address, phone number, professional location, and portfolio/GitHub or live-project links if available. Do not invent or add placeholder contact details. This is important for recruiter usability and application completion.
3. In the Experience section under "Teaching Assistant," expand the single bullet using only the supported facts. For example: "Supported approximately 30 first-year students across one semester of web development lab sessions, answering implementation questions and explaining web-development concepts." Remove the second clause if the candidate did not actually do those activities; the current entry is too sparse to demonstrate mentoring potential.
4. In the Tidewatch project, make the testing evidence more searchable and precise without claiming unsupported end-to-end testing. For example, change "Tested the app with NVDA and VoiceOver" to "Performed manual screen-reader testing with NVDA and VoiceOver" and retain the existing "Jest" technology. This clearly separates accessibility testing from automated unit testing.
5. In the Experience section under Harbourline Media, consolidate the two overlapping accessibility/component bullets into one stronger, non-repetitive set of bullets. For example: "Built a keyboard- and screen-reader-friendly image gallery for article pages using React; documented the component in Storybook." and "Used Jest and React Testing Library for automated unit/component testing while implementing accessibility fixes on the news website." This improves clarity and keyword relevance.
6. In the Education section, add the actual expected graduation date or study period if available. Do not invent a date. "Computing — third-year student" is useful but incomplete for a recruiter assessing an early-career application.

MINOR / VALUABLE ENHANCEMENTS
7. In the Technical Skills section, change "Backend and data" to "Backend, APIs and databases" and retain "Node.js, Express, PostgreSQL". This better reflects the job's terminology while remaining truthful. Do not add NestJS, SQL beyond the PostgreSQL evidence, AWS, Docker, OWASP, Git, or Playwright because they are not supported by the candidate information.
8. In the Projects section, add the supported 2024 student hackathon as a concise project or achievement: "Placed 2nd in a 2024 student hackathon; worked in a three-person team to build a transit-delay notifier in 24 hours and developed the frontend." This provides additional evidence of teamwork, delivery under time constraints, and frontend development.
9. In the Additional Experience section, change "Run social media for a sea swimming club" to the grammatically complete "Manage social media for a sea swimming club." Add dates only if known. This is a small professionalism improvement.
10. If the candidate has actually used Git, semantic HTML, responsive layouts, or any end-to-end test tool, add those items only in the relevant Skills or Project bullets with a concrete example. The current source material does not support adding them, so they should remain absent unless verified.
